correctness.rationale: Reassessed the repaired files. During a four-step return the number of modulo-four advances of each vertex is either zero or four; any vertex visiting a nonzero state must advance, and a permanently zero vertex cannot be adjacent to a rotating one. Connectivity leaves only all rest or all rotation, with least period four in the latter case. The successor-neighbor condition is then necessary and sufficient. Fixing hub phase 0 meets each temporal orbit once, and forbidding rim color 1 in the correction matrix removes exactly the words that fail the hub. Fresh symbolic characteristic polynomial computation from the original local predicate (not the supplied certificate) gives X^9(X²+1)(X^5−X^4−2X³−2X²−X−1) and X^6(X³−X²−X−1); expansion gives the stated counts through n=12 and zero formal terms at 1 and 2. The frozen proof had a real gap: Perron–Frobenius only puts the other quintic roots below λ, not below the distinct error scale μ. In the corrected RESULT.md, the quotient Q(X) after deflation at λ has coefficients (1,a₁,a₂,a₃,a₄) in descending order, satisfying 0<a₄<a₃<a₂<a₁=λ−1. By coefficient-ratio bounds all four roots have modulus at most λ−1<μ. The cubic roots and bounded unit-circle terms thus yield O(μ^n). Reconstructing the analogous 3-color transfers gives X^4(X²+X+1)(X³−2X²−1) and X³(X−1), as in the credited formula. Exact rational sign evaluations at the printed brackets have signs −,+ for all three roots. The inequalities λ>ρ and 3λ<4ρ follow from these brackets, and 4Oₙ/4^{n+1}=Oₙ/4^n is the starting-state probability. Replay from the definitions in proof §§1–3, compute the characteristic polynomials and logarithmic traces, then use the corrected coefficient bounds in §4. No other recurrent periods or eventual basin sizes are inferred.

The quotient generating function separates the rim constraint from failure to excite the hub.
